html:
The global order is significantly reshaped today by the comprehensive victory of Democrats in the US midterm elections, marking a historic defeat for Republicans and intensifying questions around US president Donald Trump’s authority and policy directions, particularly concerning the escalating conflict with Iran. This outcome has immediately influenced White House appointments and sparked global economic shifts.

US Politics: Following their sweeping midterm triumph, which saw Democrats regain control of both the House and Senate, US president Donald Trump announced the appointment of Stephen Miller, known as an architect of his immigration crackdown, as White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. This move drew criticism from Democrats, with Chuck Schumer stating Trump "learned nothing from his historic defeat." The focus has already shifted to the 2028 presidential race, with a former Obama aide reporting "over two dozen campaigns" are eyeing a run, while Democrats also signal investigations into Trump administration corruption, including Middle East deals. A judge also blocked the construction of Trump's arch after federal agency approval.

US-Iran Tensions: The ongoing US-Iran war and its impact on the midterms are central to today’s headlines, with US Vice President JD Vance blaming the conflict and support for Israel for Republican losses, a claim rejected by Israel's UN ambassador. Tensions escalated further as Iran's IRGC reported that a US drone was shot down and two or three oil tankers were struck and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran also claiming two LUCAS drones were seized. Amid reports of the US talking to Tehran’s representatives and Trump saying they are "doing very well," the US president also threatened that he "might have to destroy what's left of the country." Russia, meanwhile, reportedly agreed to supply Iran with 90 advanced missile launchers.

Global Economy & Technology: Financial markets responded to the US election results, with global stocks falling sharply amid "big worries over AI" after the Democratic victory. Investors had been selling off tech shares due to concerns a Democrat win would mean slower AI development, with European and Asian markets following a US tech rout. Separately, three men have been charged in the US with using AI to impersonate CEOs and steal over $100 million. Elon Musk appeared to signal the end of production for the Cybertruck, making way for Cybercabs, its autonomous taxis.

European Security: Europe faced a new wave of bomb threats targeting multiple flights, leading to dozens of diversions, and several broadcasters. Irish government officials suggest these are part of a coordinated campaign of disruption. Separately, Spain's rail authorities are under a European fraud probe concerning EU funds for upgrading the railway line where the Urda rail disaster killed 69 people. France is dealing with mounting public debt and nationwide protests, including a planned €4 billion extra for education.

Middle East Regional Dynamics: Beyond the US-Iran conflict, Turkey's parliament ratified the Mecca Defense Pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, clearing the way for military support to Saudi Arabia, as Saudi-led coalition forces intercepted a Houthi-fired missile targeting the Medina region. Al Mayadeen reported Yemeni forces seized strategic sites in the Kahboub mountains east of Bab al-Mandab. Separately, Reuters, citing Syrian and US military sources, reported that Syrian training teams are heading to Saudi Arabia to assist in training Saudi and Yemeni units. Meanwhile, in Israel, Arab-led parties are in the spotlight after an inconclusive election, with their backing potentially key to unseating Netanyahu.

Other Global Developments: Pope Leo XIV embarked on a 12-day, three-country tour of South America, visiting Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, just weeks after lung cancer surgery. In Kenya, cult leader Paul Mackenzie was sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murder of 190 children and one adult. Paraguay plunged into a political crisis following the collapse of Ueno Bank, leading to the impeachment and removal of President Santiago Pena.
